unknowns: Specific fat and protein concentration ranges of interest.
Which composition changes are to be detected and on what timescale.
Whether the product is a true solution, emulsion, dispersion or slurry, and its particle size distribution.
Whether the opaque appearance is dominated by scattering or absorption.
Exact temperature range and rate of variation during production.
Process pressure and flow conditions at the intended measurement point.
Installation point, path length and distance from the spectrometer.
Required accuracy, precision, limit of detection and response time.
Reference method details and sampling protocol for the retained laboratory checks.
Whether texture variation affects optical sampling or requires special probe design.
Availability of any existing fiber links or process windows.
